$comment: Which numbers a behaviour flag needs. Data, on purpose.
MOST VALUES IN HERE ARE STILL GUESSES, and the ones that are not now say
so. A first cut chosen to be reasonable and never tuned against a patch a
person listened to is a hypothesis about music; a number derived from what
a synthesis teacher chose in order to DEMONSTRATE the effect is something
better, and the two should not look alike. So a condition may carry a
`grounding`: where its number comes from, and what it would take to
dislodge it. A condition with no `grounding` is still a guess.
They live in a data file so that tuning one is an edit somebody can review
and revert, rather than a constant buried in a compiled gate. Treat an
ungrounded number as a hypothesis about music, and when it disagrees with
a listener, the listener is right. A grounded one still loses to a
listener; it just costs an argument first.
The flags are the ones the idiom library actually carries. Two names from
the original sketch are spelled differently in the data and are the same
idea: a 'drone' is `sustained`, and 'evolving' is `spectrally_varying`.
`all_of` is the predicate. `needs` is different and load-bearing: it says
when the measurement is MEANINGFUL at all. A patch whose pitch was
trackable for 8% of the run has a `distinct_pitches` reading, and that
reading is not evidence of anything. A flag whose `needs` are unmet comes
back UNMEASURED, never failed -- rejecting a patch on a number that was
never really measured is how a gate teaches a model to game it.

melodic.means: plays a tune rather than holding a note

needs.says: a pitch could only be tracked for {actual:.0%} of the run, so there is no melody to judge either way

all_of.says: only {actual:.0f} distinct pitch(es) in the whole run; the sequencer's step values ARE the melody, so write them and make them differ
the pitch changed {actual:.0f} time(s); a melody moves more than that

rhythmic.means: there are attacks, and they land on a pulse

all_of.says: only {actual:.0f} attack(s) in the run; nothing is being struck or gated repeatedly
the attacks do not fall on a pulse (autocorrelation {actual:.2f}); clock the sequencer or the envelope from something steady

keeps_going.means: still sounding at the end of the run

all_of.says: the last half second is {actual:.2f} of the loudest moment; the patch fires once and dies rather than running

sustained.means: a held sound rather than a series of events

all_of.says: sound is present for only {actual:.0%} of the run; a sustained patch does not have gaps
{actual:.1f} attacks a second is a rhythm, not a drone
all_of.grounding: Derived, not guessed. cookbook-sc (microcosm/cookbook-sc, '3. Envelopes.sc') demonstrates a slow/pad shape as Env.adsr(1.5, 1.5, 0.5, 4) and a fast/plucked one as Env.adsr(0.3, 0.3, 0.9, 1.2). Attack+decay is 3.0s for the pad and 0.6s for the pluck, so a patch using the pad shape cannot start more than about 0.33 notes a second and one using the pluck can manage about 1.7. This threshold sits between them, which is the useful place for it: it separates the two envelope shapes a teacher chose to demonstrate the difference with. Move it only with a reason that beats that.

spectrally_varying.means: the timbre moves across the run

needs.says: only {actual:.0f} windows carried enough signal to have a spectrum, so brightness over time was not really measured

any_of.says: brightness spans {actual:.2f} octaves; nothing is opening or closing
any_of.grounding: Derived, not guessed. cookbook-sc ('2. Filters.sc') sweeps a filter over MouseY.kr(110, 16000) to demonstrate what sweeping sounds like -- a span of 7.2 octaves. This asks for 0.5, about a fourteenth of that, which is a deliberate floor rather than a target: a patch's CENTROID moves far less than its cutoff, because the harmonics the filter removes were only part of the spectrum. If this ever rejects a patch a listener calls evolving, it is too high.

needs.says: {actual:.0f} attacks is too few to say whether the tempo is moving

all_of.says: the gaps between attacks trend {actual:+.2f} across the run; nothing is speeding up

varies_timing.means: the events are not on a grid

needs.says: {actual:.0f} attacks is too few to say whether the timing varies

all_of.says: the attacks are metronomically even (cv {actual:.2f}); nothing is humanising or randomising the timing
the timing is not varying, it is accelerating (trend {actual:+.2f}), which is a different thing

unmetered.means: sounds happen, but not to a pulse

needs.says: {actual:.0f} attacks is too few to say whether there is a metre

all_of.says: the attacks fall on a clear pulse (autocorrelation {actual:.2f}) when the idiom asks for free time
